paragraphs: Kol akila ushetiyya hamulla yoter mitztzad habberur hannaaseh bah tiqqenu bah berakot yoter, lekak akilat hallechem shehi meulla yoter bimleket habberur tiqqenu lepaneha shette berakot shehem "al netilat yadayim" v",hammotzi", uleachareha chamesh berakot shehem arba debirkat hammazon veachat shel hakkos, vaakila shel shibat hamminin kesheokel mine mezonot, o perot haetz dachamishsha minin hoil veenah meulla akila zo kaakilat hallechem haggamur, lo tiqqenu bah ella beraka achat baacharona ak hi meen shalosh berakot debirkat hammazon, vaakila shel perot dishar ilanot o perot haadama ubasar vedagim vekayyotze digria meotah akila shel shibat hamminim shennishtabbecha bahem eretz yisrael lo tiqqenu bahem beraka meen shalosh ella beraka shel "bore nepashot rabbot":

Laken chamishsha mine perot shehem mishshibat hamminim shennishtabbecha bahem eretz yisrael im akal mehem kazzayit shehu tisha deraham mebarek leachareha beraka meen shalosh shehi al haetz veal peri haetz veku' vechotem venodeh lak Adonai elohenu al haaretz veal happerot baruk atta Adonai al haaretz veal happerot, vachamishsha minim ellu sheggadelu beeretz yisrael atzmah ben im okelam beeretz yisrael ben im okelam bechutz laaretz chotem venodeh veku' al haaretz veal peroteha baruk atta Adonai al haaretz veal peroteha, veim okel mine mezonot sheggadelu beeretz yisrael atzmah chotem al haaretz veal michya veal kalkalatah veken hu haddin beyayin achar sheshshata keshiur shetztzarik beraka meen shalosh al hayyayin shel chutz laaretz yachtom venodeh lak Adonai elohenu al haaretz veal peri haggapen baruk atta Adonai al haaretz veal peri haggapen, veal yayin shel eretz yisrael yachtom venodeh veku' al haaretz veal peri gapnah baruk atta Adonai al haaretz veal peri gapna:

clarification.explanation: The more superior the process of extraction (berur) accomplished through an eating, the more blessings were instituted for it: eating bread (the most superior) — two blessings before it (netilat yadayim, hamotzi) and five after it (the four of Birkat HaMazon plus the blessing over the cup); eating the seven species or grain foods — one blessing at the end (me’ein shalosh); and other fruits/foods — ‘Borei nefashot rabot’ alone. For the five kinds among the seven species, when one eats a kezayit of them — one blesses afterward me’ein shalosh (‘al ha’etz ve’al pri ha’etz’…); if they grew in the Land of Israel — one concludes ‘al ha’aretz ve’al peroteha’; grain foods from the Land of Israel — ‘al ha’aretz ve’al hamichyah ve’al hakalkalah’; wine from outside the Land — ‘al ha’aretz ve’al pri hagafen’; and wine from the Land of Israel — ‘al ha’aretz ve’al pri gafnah.’
takeaways: The final blessing depends on the level of the eating: bread (seven blessings total), the seven species/grain foods (me’ein shalosh), other foods (Borei nefashot rabot).
The wording of me’ein shalosh changes slightly according to the fruit’s origin (Land of Israel or outside it).

paragraphs: Shiur kazzayit lebarek acharayv beraka acharona hen meen shalosh hen "bore nepashot rabbot" shehu tisha drh"m kol zeh hu baakila, abal bishtiyya ben yayin ben mayim ushear mashqin en mebarekin beraka acharona ella ad sheshshoteh rebiit shehu z"k drh"m, ak yesh choleqin usebira lehu gam bemashqin chiyyub beraka acharona hu betisha deraham v"g dela qayma lan haki mishshum sapeq berakot lehaqel yere shamayim yizzaher shello yabi atzmo beyadayim lide sapeq zeh, ella o yishteh pachot mittisha deraham velo yebarek lekulle alema, o yishteh z"k drh"m vibarek lekulle alema:

clarification.explanation: The measure of a kezayit for an after-blessing (me’ein shalosh or Borei nefashot rabot) is nine dirhams — this applies to eating only; for drinking — one does not bless an after-blessing except after a revi’it, which is twenty-seven dirhams. There are those who disagree and hold that for beverages too, the measure of a kezayit (nine dirhams) suffices, but the halachah is not so; one who fears Heaven should be careful not to enter this doubt — he should drink less than nine dirhams (and then not bless according to any opinion), or drink twenty-seven dirhams (and then bless according to all opinions).
takeaways: An after-blessing on eating applies from the measure of a kezayit (nine dirhams); on drinking — only from the measure of a revi’it (twenty-seven dirhams).

paragraphs: Bibraka meen shalosh hen shel mezonot hen shel yayin hen shel chameshet hamminin deeretz yisrael, tzarik lehazkir meen hamora beshabbat veyom tob verosh chodesh veim shakach en machazirin oto, veim amar ki atta tob umetib lakkol velo hizkir meen hamora lo yazkir od, ukemo deqayma lan bebirkat hammazon deim hitchil beraka rebiit shub eno yakol lehazkir meen hamora ken haddin bazeh, yaan ki atta tob umetib hu meen beraka rebiit d"g deqorin libraka zo meen shalosh hinneh hi beemet meen arba veqareu otah meen shalosh mippene dehashshalosh hemma deorayeta lekak niqret al shemam ken hu sebarat eliyya raba siman r"ch seip qatan k', mihu harab hammaggihha bechesed laalapim siman r"ch mechuddash d' irer bazeh vekatab deyesh lechalleq yeuyyan sham, veal ken haaleti bsh"q mqbtzyl kevan deamar ki atta tob umetib lakkol lo yazkir meen hamora beperush ella yeharher haddebarim belibbo veaach"k yachtom:

clarification.explanation: In the blessing me’ein shalosh — whether of grain foods, of wine, or of the five kinds of fruit of the Land of Israel — one must mention the special occasion on Shabbat, Yom Tov, and Rosh Chodesh; and if one forgot, one does not go back. And if one has already said ‘ki atah tov u’metiv lakol’ without having mentioned the special occasion — one should not mention it anymore, just as in Birkat HaMazon, if one has begun the fourth blessing, one can no longer mention the special occasion. The reason: ‘ki atah tov u’metiv’ is like a fourth blessing — for even though this blessing is called me’ein shalosh, it is in truth me’ein arba, and is named after the three because they are from the Torah (per the Eliyah Rabbah); however, the annotator in Chesed LaAlafim challenged this and made a distinction. Therefore the Ben Ish Chai concluded (in Makabtziel): if one has already said ‘ki atah tov u’metiv lakol’ — one should not mention the special occasion explicitly, but should reflect on the matter in his heart and then conclude the blessing.
takeaways: Me’ein shalosh — one mentions the special occasion on Shabbat/Yom Tov/Rosh Chodesh; if one forgot — one does not go back.
If one has already said ‘ki atah tov u’metiv lakol’ (which is like a fourth blessing) — one should not mention it explicitly, but reflect on it in one’s heart and conclude.

paragraphs: Akal perot mishshibat hamminim vegam mine mezonot vegam shata yayin yiklol bibraka acharona lishlashettam yachad, veyaqdim hammichya veaach"k haggapen veaach"k haetz:

clarification.explanation: One who ate fruits of the seven species, and also grain foods, and also drank wine — includes all three in one blessing (me’ein shalosh), giving precedence to ‘hamichyah,’ then ‘hagafen,’ then ‘ha’etz.’
takeaways: One who ate grain foods, wine, and fruits of the seven species — blesses one blessing including all of them, in the order: grain foods, wine, tree fruit.

paragraphs: Kol haokalin mitztarepin lekazzayit, abal akila ushetiyya en mitztarepin, umihu pat hashsheruya bemashqeh mitztarep hammashqeh habbalua betokah leshiur kazzayit: veha deamerinan kol haokalin mitztarepin lekazzayit haynu davqa lebarek "bore nepashot rabbot", abal libraka meen shalosh im akal chatzi zayit mechameshet hamminin vachatzi zayit shear perot lo yebarek meen shalosh ella yebarek "bore nepashot rabbot" veayyen tob ayin lehaggaon chida" za"l dap m"d, vehu haddin im akal chatzi zayit mechameshet hamminin vachatzi zayit mezonot o chatzi zayit pat en mitztarepin vibarek "bore nepashot rabbot" abal chamishsha mine perot shel shibat hamminim mitztarepin sheim akal chatzi zayit anabim vachatzi zayit teenim o rimmonim o zetim o temarim mitztarepim zeh im zeh lebarek meen shalosh, veim akal chatzi zayit mezonot vachatzi zayit pat yebarek meen shalosh:

clarification.explanation: Different foods combine together to reach the measure of a kezayit (for the purpose of ‘Borei nefashot rabot’ only), but eating and drinking do not combine with each other (except for bread soaked in a beverage, where the absorbed beverage combines). Regarding the me’ein shalosh blessing: fruits of the seven species combine with each other (for example, half a kezayit of grapes and half a kezayit of figs), but they do not combine with fruits/grain foods that are not of the seven species; half a kezayit of grain food and half a kezayit of bread do combine for me’ein shalosh.
takeaways: Grain foods and different eatings combine for ‘Borei nefashot rabot’; for me’ein shalosh — only within matching groups (the seven species among themselves, or grain foods with bread).

paragraphs: Im akal perot shebbirkatan meen shalosh vegam akal perot shebbirkatan "bore nepashot rabbot" "p sheakal mikkol echad shiur kazzayit en tzarik lebarek "bore nepashot rabbot" deellu niptarim bibraka meen shalosh shemmebarek atta:

clarification.explanation: One who ate both fruits whose blessing is me’ein shalosh and fruits whose blessing is ‘Borei nefashot rabot’ (a kezayit measure of each) — need not bless ‘Borei nefashot rabot’ separately, because they are exempted by the me’ein shalosh blessing that he blesses.
takeaways: The me’ein shalosh blessing also exempts other foods whose blessing is ‘Borei nefashot rabot,’ if eaten together.

paragraphs: Akal chatzi zayit veshaha vechazar veakal chatzi zayit im en mehatchalat chatzi zayit harishon ad sop chatzi zayit haacharon shiur akilat peras shehu shiur shelosh betzim dehaynu n"d deraham hare shette akilot ellu mitztarepin umebarek beraka acharona, veim lav en mitztarepin velo yebarek, v"g deyesh choleqin usebira lehu baakila shel reshut im akal kashshiur apillu im shaha kede akilat peras mebarek beraka acharona, dela ittemar hay dina ella beakil choba kegon matztza delel pesach o kazzayit pat delayla rishona dechag bassukka mikkol maqom ha qayma lan sapeq berakot lehaqel, veayyen zekor leabraham cheleq g' baqqunetres acharon veod shear acharonim shello huzkeru sham, umihu nireh li sheyyebarek beli shem umalkut viharher shem umalkut belibbo, veim era lo kak veepshar lo lehashlim shiur belo shehiyya ulebarek tabo alayv beraka, vekol zeh baakila abal bishtiyya im shata meat veshaha veaach"k hishlim hashshiur im yesh mittechilla vead sop shiur shetiyyat rebiit en mitztarepin:

clarification.explanation: One who ate half a kezayit, paused, and then ate another half a kezayit — if the total elapsed time (from the beginning of the first eating to the end of the second) is less than the measure of ‘achilat peras’ (about the size of three eggs, roughly 54 dirhams) — the two eatings combine for the after-blessing; if more — they do not combine, and one does not bless (or blesses without mentioning God’s name and sovereignty, reflecting on the name and sovereignty in his heart); and if he is able to complete the measure without pausing and then bless, it is praiseworthy to do so. There are those who disagree and hold that this law (that a long pause invalidates the combination) was stated only regarding an obligatory eating, such as matzah on the night of Pesach or a kezayit of bread on the first night of Sukkot — but for an optional eating, even if one paused for the duration of achilat peras, the eatings combine and one blesses the after-blessing; but despite this dispute, in practice the stricter opinion is followed, because doubts about blessings are resolved leniently. In drinking — it combines only if the entire drinking took place within the measure of drinking a revi’it.
takeaways: Too long a pause (more than ‘achilat peras’) between two eatings of the same food invalidates the combination for the after-blessing.

Some hold that for optional eating (unlike obligatory eating such as matzah on the night of Pesach), the pause does not invalidate the combination, but in practice the stricter view is followed out of doubt about blessings.

paragraphs: Hammotzetz perot chashib akila veshiur bikzayit, vehaynu davqa bemotzetzam "y leisa shennotenam bepiv dekevan shetztzarik hu lilos beshinnayv dayenin leh keokel veshiure bikzayit, abal metzitza sheen bah leisa kegon hammotzetz prtq"l (tpv"z) o nrn"g (peri hadar qatan, chimmutz) vekayyotze shettopes happeri beyado umotzetzo deen bazeh leisa hare zeh dino kishtiyya, vaapillu im matzatz shiur rebiit lo yebarek beraka acharona yaan ki bishtiyya baenan shello yishheh mittechilla vead sop shiur shetiyyat rebiit vehammotzetz i epshar sheyyimtzotz shiur rebiit velo yishheh yoter mikkede shetiyyat rebiit, veal ken kol peri sheen motzetzo "y leisa en mebarek beraka acharona apillu im motzetz harbeh veayin qol eliyyahu siman z' yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation: Sucking the juice of a fruit is considered eating (with the measure of a kezayit) only if it involves chewing (placing it in the mouth and chewing). But sucking without chewing (such as sucking an orange by hand without placing it in the mouth to chew) is treated as drinking — therefore even if one sucked the measure of a revi’it, one does not bless an after-blessing, because it is impossible to suck in this way without pausing for too long.
takeaways: Sucking a fruit with chewing — is treated as eating (kezayit); sucking without chewing — is treated as drinking, and does not reach an after-blessing (because it takes too long).

paragraphs: En lebarek beraka acharona al mashqeh cham kegon qhvv" (qapeh) o gy"y (th) vekayyotze, mippene sheen shotim mehem shiur rebiit bilti shehaya shehu shiur shetiyyat rebiit mechamat shehem chammim, vehu haddin leshoteh mayim qarim bimot hachorep shemmukrach lishtot meat meat mippene haqqerirut veshoheh bishtiyyato harbeh:

clarification.explanation: One does not bless an after-blessing over a hot beverage (coffee, tea), because it is impossible to drink the measure of a revi’it from it in one continuous span (due to the heat, one drinks it slowly, little by little). The same applies to very cold water in winter that causes one to drink slowly.
takeaways: A hot beverage (or one too cold) that causes slow drinking — has no after-blessing on it, because one cannot drink a revi’it in one continuous span.

paragraphs: Im lo haya bedato leekol ella raq chatzi shiur ki ratza leekol raq tappucha echad shehu chatzi shiur vehebiu lo veakal veaach"k nitavva lattappucha acher vehebiu lo uberak alayv vaakalo "p shello haya mittechillat akilat tappucha rishon ad sop akilat tappucha sheni shiur akilat peras im kol zeh nistappequ happoseqim im mitztarepim b' akilot ellu lebarek beraka acharona venishar haddabar bispeq berakot, lekak lo yabi atzmo ledabar zeh ella im ken yokal bashsheniyya shiur shalem, veim abar veakal veen lo od lehashlim hashshiur hare zeh yebarek beli shem umalkut viharher shem umalkut belibbo:

clarification.explanation: One who intended to eat only half a measure (one apple), and afterward changed his mind and ate an additional apple (with a separate blessing) — there is doubt as to whether the two eatings combine for the after-blessing, even if they were in sequence (within the measure of achilat peras). Therefore he should not bring himself into this doubt, but should eat a full measure the second time, or bless without mentioning God’s name and sovereignty if this has already occurred.
takeaways: Eating that was not originally planned as a whole (half-and-half with separate intentions) — is in doubt regarding the after-blessing; it is preferable to complete a full measure.

paragraphs: Shata yayin vegam shear mashqin eno mebarek "bore nepashot rabbot" al hammashqin debirkat al haggepen potartan veim shata hammayim o shear mashqin qodem sheshshata hayyayin yesh omerim deen al haggepen potartan veyesh omerim degam bazeh poteret, laken tzarik lehizzaher shello yabi atzmo lispeq berakot vibarek "bore nepashot rabbot" al hammayim o al shear mashqin qodem sheyyishteh hayyayin veim lo asa ken yebarek "bore nepashot rabbot" beli shem umalkut mishshum sapeq berakot lehaqel:

clarification.explanation: One who drank wine and also other beverages — does not bless ‘Borei nefashot rabot’ on the beverages, because the blessing of ‘hagefen’ exempts them. But if he drank other beverages (water and the like) before drinking the wine, there is a dispute: some say that the blessing of hagefen does not exempt them retroactively, and some say that it exempts them even in this case too. Therefore one must be careful not to enter a doubt about blessings, and should bless ‘Borei nefashot rabot’ over the water or other beverages before drinking the wine. And if he was not careful about this, he should bless ‘Borei nefashot rabot’ without mentioning God’s name and sovereignty, because of the doubt.
takeaways: After wine, one does not bless ‘Borei nefashot rabot’ on other beverages — the blessing of hagefen exempts them.
If one drinks another beverage before the wine, it is preferable to bless ‘Borei nefashot rabot’ on it immediately, before drinking the wine, so as not to enter a doubt.
If one was not careful and already drank a beverage before the wine, one should bless ‘Borei nefashot rabot’ without mentioning God’s name and sovereignty.

paragraphs: Im akal o shata kashshiur vetekep umiyyad heqio eno mebarek beraka acharona veayyen acharonim:

clarification.explanation: One who ate or drank the requisite measure and immediately vomited it — does not bless an after-blessing.
takeaways: Immediate vomiting after eating/drinking exempts one from the after-blessing.

paragraphs: Beraka meen shalosh yizzaher lebarek otah meyushshab, mippene deyesh omerim shehahi deorayeta, vehammachmir lebarek meen shalosh beenayim segurot kemo birkat hammazon tabo alayv beraka:

clarification.explanation: The me’ein shalosh blessing should be blessed while seated (there are those who hold that it is from the Torah), and one who is stringent to bless it with closed eyes, like Birkat HaMazon — a blessing will come upon him.
takeaways: Me’ein shalosh — is blessed while seated (and preferably also with closed eyes).

paragraphs: En adam oneh amen achar birkotayv ella im ken amar shette berakot o yoter az yomar besop habberakot amen, velaken hambarek birkot hahaptara oneh amen achar birkot hahaptora, vehashshomea echad miyyisrael mebarek achat mikkol habberakot apillu shello shama kullah mittechilla veal zeh chayyab laanot amen, vikavven haoneh gam al hambarek lehotzio yede chobat aniyyat amen, velaken tzarik laanot beqol kede sheyyishma hambarek vegam tzarik sheyyitkavven hambarek latzet yede choba, ak yizzaher haoneh shello yarim qolo beumman yoter min hambarek vehazzohar haqqadosh hechmir meod beonesh hashshomea beraka veeno oneh amen laken im hambarek al ezeh dabar leatzmo roeh dehashshomein mezalzelim beumman veen onin, tob sheyyebarek belachash kede shello yishmeu habberaka veyabou lide mikshol vekannizkar bechesed laalapim siman rt"v ot g':

clarification.explanation: One does not answer ‘Amen’ after one’s own blessings, unless one said two or more blessings in sequence — in which case one answers ‘Amen’ at the end of all of them (such as one who blesses the blessings of the Haftarah). One who hears a blessing from a fellow Jew — even if he did not hear it all from the beginning — is obligated to answer ‘Amen’ (aloud, so that the one blessing can hear, and with intent to fulfill the listener’s obligation) — but not louder than the one blessing. If the listeners treat the matter with contempt and do not answer ‘Amen,’ it is better to bless quietly so that they will not come to stumble.
takeaways: One answers ‘Amen’ to one’s own blessing only if one said two consecutive blessings; answering ‘Amen’ to another’s blessing is obligatory even without hearing all of it.

paragraphs: Kesheshshomea achar mitpallel al dabar o mebarek leyisrael apillu belo hazkarat hashshem chayyab laanot amen, ulekak tzarik laanot amen achar harachaman bebirkat hammazon, veken tzarik laanot amen kesheoseh hashlicha tzibbur mi shebberak laqqahal, veken yaanu amen kesheomer shelicha tzibbur qodem musap bashshemini atzeret ubeyom rishon shel pesach: "begishme ora tair adama veku'" "betille ora tair adama veku'" veken bislichot kesheomer "elohenu shebbashshamayim veku'" yaanu hatztzibbur amen, veken kol kayyotze bazeh:

clarification.explanation: One who hears a person praying or blessing on behalf of Israel (even without mention of God’s name) is obligated to answer ‘Amen’; therefore one answers ‘Amen’ after ‘HaRachaman’ in Birkat HaMazon, after the ‘Mi shebeirach’ of the prayer leader, and in the wording of the Selichot that contain similar requests.
takeaways: One answers ‘Amen’ also on requests/blessings for the congregation that do not mention God’s name (HaRachaman, Mi shebeirach, Selichot).

paragraphs: Yilmad banayv haqqetannim sheyyaanu amen, demiyyad shehattinoq oneh amen yesh lo cheleq laolam habba, vetinoqot asher mebarekim chayyab haadam laanot acharehem amen, veraq im hem lomedim nosach habberakot derek limmud kede lehitlammed en onin acharehem amen, vekol hambarek beraka sheenah tzerika asur laanot acharayv amen, vekol hammeshanneh mimmatbea shettabeu chaza"l bibrakot bedabar shemmeakkeb en onin acharayv amen, vekol shekken im dilleg shem umalkut bibraka shettiqqenu bah shem umalkut, daapillu im lo dilleg ella tebat haolam en onin acharayv amen:

clarification.explanation: One should teach young children to answer ‘Amen’ — the very act of a child answering ‘Amen’ earns him a share in the World to Come, and one is obligated to answer after their blessing. But if they are merely reciting the wording of the blessings (without genuine intent to bless), as a form of learning — one does not answer after them. One does not answer ‘Amen’ after an unnecessary blessing, or a blessing whose formula was altered in an invalidating way, and all the more so if one omitted God’s name and sovereignty (or even just the word ‘ha’olam’).
takeaways: Children are taught to answer ‘Amen’ (it earns them merit); one does not answer to a blessing recited merely for practice, an unnecessary blessing, or a corrupted blessing (especially missing God’s name and sovereignty).
